courseTitle: NativeScript + Angular: Build Native iOS, Android & Web Apps

cues.en: Well, to get the input here, we can use a convenient feature added by ANGULAR, we can add a local
reference to any HTML element here by adding a hash tag and then some name of your choice like person
name.
But you can name whoever you want and I'll name it person name El, because it really is a reference
to the element, not to the value in there, but to the whole element, because you could add this to
any element, not just to inputs.
Now this is a reference which is now only available in this template by default, but that's no problem.
We can pass it as an argument to our button.
And actually I don't pass the whole element, but I know it's the element on our input.
So I can just pass personell dot value here to access to value property of this element, because this
input element, the underlying JavaScript object, which is implicitly stored in here, has a value
property which holds the current value we entered.
So now we know we passed the current value of this input to uncreate person and therefore back into
component.
We can expect this as an argument person name.
And again, it's a good idea to define the type.
So we add colon string because we know it will be a string.
It's the value of an input element that always is a string.
And then we could output created a person plus person name to output that name as well.
If you now say that and you go back to the application, if I enter Max here and click create, you
see created a person, Max.
So passing the data works as well with the help of local references.
